first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, making simplification the most directly aligned intervention and likely to improve time-to-value without immediately sacrificing price realization. Verify the onboarding result because it is central to this week's choice, and verify promotional pricing because competitor pressure makes it a consequential alternative but discounts may weaken sustainable qualified revenue. Run a guarded experiment measuring completion, activation, qualified pipeline or revenue, and retention-quality signals rather than optimizing completion alone.

final.rationale: Use this week's slot to test the shortened onboarding flow, which is directly aligned with the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline and has archived evidence of improving completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. Measure activation, qualified revenue, and retention—not completion alone—to protect sustainable long-term value. Do not pursue promotional pricing as the primary experiment: although it produced an 18% qualified-revenue lift, the 12% 30-day retention decline indicates poor first-renewal durability. Run a standard experiment with a control and guardrails for lead quality, conversion, and retention.
